decision: #891: a refused microphone aborts the voice-timbre take instead of leaving it armed at 0 %
reasoning: MicrophoneManager.startRecording() has exactly one line that sets isRecording=true; five returns and a catch leave it false. From VoiceCaptureController the live ones are the #890 placeholder-format refusal and the catch around audioEngine.start(). Both returned with no tap installed, so no sample could ever arrive and the take sat on .capturing 0 % until the user cancelled - on a phone indistinguishable from a hang, and exactly the state the founder's #890 device probe would land in. begin() now re-reads mic.isRecording after starting it; hasPermission is the discriminator so the legitimate permission wait is untouched. The abort deliberately skips releaseMic(), whose stopRecording() would write a three-rung stop ladder for a mic that never started (#882) and release the record route a second time.
expected_outcome: The #890 device probe becomes answerable without the log: it worked, it refused visibly, or something else. No new founder ask filed (#790).

decision: #892: the applied voice profile outranks the refusal message, and both non-begin() exits clear the flag
reasoning: #891 put the refusal caption first on a false premise - that the flag can only be true with no profile applied, because Capture is the only button reaching begin(). That argues about when the flag is SET, not when it is READ: PolySynthVoice.apply(_:) installs a profile from any recalled patch carrying voiceProfileTaps (#593c), and the preset bar that does it sits directly above the row. Refusal, then a preset load, then the row shows Clear beside the text Tap Capture again - a control that is not on screen. Two independent reviewers (audio-thread, ui-state) found it the same hour.
expected_outcome: A rationale about WHERE a button renders is a claim about the view, and the view is the thing most likely to change underneath it. Branch order plus unconditional clearing in cancel() and clearApplied(), pinned by claim 6 of TheVoiceDoorFeedsTheCaptureTests.

decision: #893: the refusal marker becomes a streak COUNT, so a second refusal in a row looks different
reasoning: #891 made it a Bool. A second refusal then rendered byte-identical to the first - same sentence, same button, same phase, all inside one synchronous tap - so the player got no evidence the tap did anything. The founder's open #890 device probe asks for a capture immediately after launch TWICE IN A ROW; with a Bool that probe could not distinguish refused-again from the-button-is-dead, which is the exact confusion #891 existed to end.
expected_outcome: A count is the smallest thing that changes when the state repeats. Cleared where a run genuinely ends (completed take, cancel, clear), never in begin() - resetting at arm time would make in-a-row impossible while looking like hygiene, which is why that absence is a pinned counterweight. The breadcrumb carries the count so the exported log answers the probe without the screen.

decision: #894: a rename sweep must grep the ARGUMENTS FOR the code, not only the code
reasoning: #893 renamed micUnavailable to micRefusals and correctly moved four guard needles - but left two RATIONALES describing the deleted line. cancel()'s comment still said the write was always-already-false because begin() clears the flag, which #893 had just removed, contradicting the property doc seventy lines up in the same file; the guard's failure message repeated it. That write is now load-bearing: refusal, tap Capture again, the mic starts, Cancel - without it the caption reports a failed microphone after a take that did start.
expected_outcome: Both texts corrected to say load-bearing with the reachable sequence spelled out. Also: claim 7's ingest window ran to end of file so a reset hoisted to the top of ingest passed identically - now bounded to the completion branch and proven with a negative control. And the header's derived evaluation figure was deleted rather than corrected: unlike the statement count it has no command behind it.

decision: #895: the denied-permission hang is closed, and the flag that could have reported it was lying since launch
reasoning: Three slices removed a 0% hang and none removed it for a user who had DENIED the microphone: iOS shows no prompt for that user, startRecording returns immediately, hasPermission stays false and the abort - which asks granted? - never fired. MicrophoneManager.permissionDenied could have said so but was written only inside the request callback, so at launch it read not-denied while the system said denied. Nobody caught it because the flag had ZERO readers repo-wide - an unread flag cannot be observed to lie.
expected_outcome: checkPermission derives the flag from the system status (the CameraRPPGBioPublisher shape) and runs before startRecording's guard so a Settings change lands on the next tap; begin() tests denied before granted; undetermined stays a wait, pinned by a negative assertion because collapsing the two checks reads like tidy deduplication and would abort every new user's first capture.

decision: #896: all three microphone permission states end the take; the undetermined one was the hang
reasoning: Four slices removed a 0% hang and the most common instance survived all of them: undetermined permission. #891 wrote that the wait RESOLVES by itself, #892 retracted it for denied only, #895 re-inspected the state space and signed the rest off. Measured: requestPermission's continuation writes hasPermission and nothing else (since #825 it starts nothing), startRecording has exactly one production caller which has already returned, and nothing observes hasPermission. The user taps Allow and the row sits at 0% under a caption claiming a live capture.
expected_outcome: One gate, one teardown, three recorded reasons. Aborting costs one extra tap after answering the alert instead of a hang escapable only by Cancel; auto-resume on the grant needs a callback this manager does not have and is a later slice. The guard assertion that forbade the fix was deleted: it rested on the same false premise AND was unreachable for the edit it named.

decision: #897: the abort reaches VoiceOver, and a window bounded by a guessed number is a latent red
reasoning: Five slices made the take's failure visible and none made it perceivable: every abort returns to .idle, so the Capture button keeps its label, hint and value - a VoiceOver user gets no change on the focused control and the new sentence is an unfocused sibling Text. The announced text is the caption itself, because a hand-written second string drifts the first time either is reworded. Separately, the new claim went red on its own correct code: SourceText.codeOnly blanks a comment's text but keeps its indentation, so a prefix(N) window is spent on whitespace.
expected_outcome: Announcement gated on the aborted phase, with a counterweight forbidding a string literal. All three prefix(N) windows in the guard replaced by anchored ones - measured headroom had been 703 and 1303 characters, about 24 and 45 comment lines. Device probe filed: a green bundle proves the call is written, not that the system speaks it.

decision: #898: a prefix(N) window over source text is a latent red; measured 37 sites, converted the two thin ones
reasoning: SourceText.codeOnly blanks a comment's text but keeps its indentation (it must - guards assert on the relative order of matches, so lines are preserved). A stripped doc line still costs 8 to 28 characters, so every character-counted window is spent partly on whitespace and prose written above the asserted line walks the needle out of the window. Found in #897 when a new claim went red on its own correct code. Measured across the bundle: 37 sites, two with margins of 140 and 176 characters.
expected_outcome: scripts/window-margins.py makes the remaining 35 a list rather than a hunt; SourceText.codeWindow counts CODE lines for windows with no stable end anchor; a real anchor stays the preferred repair. The 35 are a migration, not a slice (#460).

decision: #899: reviewer pass on #898 - a TIGHTER window made a guard WEAKER, and four of #898's numbers were wrong in the flattering direction
reasoning: A window fails in two directions: too small is red on correct code (the #897 finding), too large is green on broken code. #898 reasoned about the first only. The MIDI guard's needle startIfNeeded() also matches its own declaration eleven code lines below; the old 300-character window paid ~272 characters of blanked comments to stay clear of it, and counting code lines skipped exactly that padding - simulated, the false-GREEN headroom fell from about 9 code lines to ONE. Separately: 37 sites overstated the fault line (the shape occurs 35 times, but the mechanism needs SourceText.codeOnly, which only 16 of them use); the blanked-line width 8 to 28 was guessed (modal 4, range 0 to 30); and the megaphone conversion was booked with a false reason, since that file uses its own line-deleting stripper.
expected_outcome: An unambiguous needle removes the hazard at any budget (holds to 40+, simulated) - the repair is never lowering the budget. codeWindow fixed for lines: 0 and for CRLF (.whitespaces excludes carriage return). window-margins.py selftest 4 to 9 cases; --thin now says a quiet run is not an all-clear. Ledger and source rationales corrected rather than dropped (#167).

decision: #900: the throwing start exit released its ROUTE and kept its GRAPH
reasoning: MicrophoneManager.startRecording's catch has released the record route since #299 and nothing else; audioEngine, inputNode and complexDFT stayed. That only became live with #891: before it the user's unavoidable cancel ran stopRecording(), which nils all three, and since #891 the abort path returns without that detour - so the FFT scratch allocation and a stopped engine live on until the next start. Severity re-measured and LOWER than reported: the #877 TRAP note in stopRecording weighs this same half-built state and calls it harmless, so it is a lifetime defect, not a crash path.
expected_outcome: Three nils in the catch, and the tap deliberately NOT removed: only audioEngine.start() can throw after the tap is installed, so the engine there is never running, and touching inputNode on a dead engine is the isInputConnToConverter family. Guard testTheThrowingStartExitDropsItsHalfBuiltGraph pins the three nils plus a counterweight forbidding a tap removal at that point; driven in Python against both trees. Whether the memory actually returns is an Instruments question and is not claimed.

decision: #901: reviewer pass on #900 - a NOT-TOUCH note whose premise my own slice had just falsified
reasoning: Five findings, none HIGH, and three of them are the expensive prose class. #900's new comment cited the #877 TRAP note as its authority while making that note's scenario unreachable (a thrown start no longer reaches stopRecording with a tapped engine) - #167: a not-touch note with a false premise is worse than none. #900 also moved an unrunged AVAudioEngine deallocation onto the failure path with no sentence beside it, so a reader would blame the route release two blocks below. My own section-3 grading was wrong in the HARSH direction: the three nil assertions are REGRESSIONS, not anchor absence, because the extraction succeeds on the parent. The guard's to: anchor was a latent false red. And complexDFT is a vDSP DFT setup handle, not scratch memory.
expected_outcome: Notes corrected in place rather than dropped; the #877 guidance survives and one half is now stronger. The guard re-anchors on releaseRecordRoute, which is immune to an inserted #if AND carries an ordering guarantee nobody had written down: the nils must stand BEFORE the route release, so the engine is deallocated while the session is still playAndRecord. All pinned counts and the neighbouring ladder window re-driven green on both trees.

decision: #902: releaseRecordRoute had two EXITS but three OUTCOMES, and eight try? call sites swallowed the third
reasoning: #888 gave the method one breadcrumb per exit. A THROWN downgrade is a third outcome that shared the successful one's line, and eight of the thirteen release call sites are try? (every #299 failure path), so the error vanished: the log read lowering then whatever came next, indistinguishable from success. That is the #882 defect the same claim was written to prevent, one level further in. The fix deliberately does not re-insert the owner (a phantom holder would block every future downgrade - the #838b stale-ref trap) and deliberately does not retry, because downgradeToPlaybackAfterRecording clears recordingRouteNeeded BEFORE its throwing setCategory, so the next configureAudioSession lowers the category itself. Only visibility was missing.
expected_outcome: One do/catch, one unnumbered state line, the error re-thrown so no call site changes behaviour. The guard that pinned the count was raised from 2 to 3 in the same commit and its message now names the three OUTCOMES rather than the two exits. The failure line deliberately avoids the phrase route stays up, which belongs to the early-return line and is separately pinned - a second line carrying it would have satisfied that claim for the wrong reason (#367), caught before shipping.

decision: #903: reviewer pass on #902 - a twelfth guard over the same file had been red for thirteen commits
reasoning: Two HIGH findings, both re-measured by hand. (1) A breadcrumb-count pin on AudioConfiguration.swift said 8; it was correct at bd38cc3~1, became 11 when #888 added three route: lines without touching it, and 12 with #902. #888's message said the tool still derives exactly 8 ladders - the diag-ladder count, a different quantity sharing the number. Nobody noticed because the pipeline reports failure on every push, so a genuinely red guard is indistinguishable from the host dying. #902's own message claimed all eleven neighbouring claims were green: this is the twelfth and it counts the line #902 added - the #453 to #477 rule reproduced exactly. (2) #902 justified not retrying with a self-heal that does not exist: configureAudioSession has four callers and none is a routine transition, so after a thrown downgrade the session can sit on playAndRecord with an empty owner set for the rest of the process. Also: eight of thirteen call sites was invented (it is nine of twelve), the new line bypassed this file's own sanitiser for OS-supplied strings, and two doc sentences still named a latency-change caller removed by #675.
expected_outcome: Pin raised to 12 with the arithmetic spelled out; the self-heal claim replaced by what actually may repair it, with the honest admission that neither path is guaranteed; the counts corrected in source, guard, session log and decision log; the error string wrapped in sanitisedRoute with its own claim. recordingRouteNeeded stays false on the failure path - its only reader is the branch that re-applies playAndRecord, so setting it true would turn the two surviving reconfigure callers from repair into cement.

decision: #904: a checker for count pins, because #903's finding was a genus and not a case
reasoning: #903 found a count pin red on a correct tree for thirteen commits. The follow-up question is not which other number is wrong but how many such pins exist and whether they all hold - which nobody can check reliably by hand, and which CI cannot show because the pipeline reports failure on every push, so a genuinely red guard looks like a dying host. scripts/count-pins.py reads two pin shapes, resolves the pinned source via the let-binding, strips comments with the shared port imported from window-margins.py rather than a second copy, and does the arithmetic. First pass over the live tree: 55 pins checked, two red, in opposite directions - a fifth helper caller nobody counted, and a pause site #823 had turned into a stop.
expected_outcome: Both reds fixed, and their INSTRUCTIONS rewritten: the two counts were told to move together, which stopped being true once helper calls appeared without the pause line - a pin whose instruction is wrong is worse than one whose number is, because the number is caught by the next run and the instruction is obeyed. Validated against its own known positive per section 4: pointed at the tree that carried the #903 defect it reports exactly one red with the true numbers, and is clean on the repaired tree. Interpolated needles are a hard exclusion after the first draft raised a false alarm on its first run (#665).

decision: #905: reviewer pass on #904 - the checker was reading the smaller half of its own subject
reasoning: Three HIGH findings, all re-measured. (1) The tool demanded the bare name occurrences, so it never saw the codeOccurrences spelling - the LARGER half, 73 vs 51, and the one dead-needles.py already parses - while printing a total that read like a census; the binding regexes also rejected a labelled argument, which produced ten of the twenty-five unresolved. Two regex characters took it from 55 to 136 pins checked with no new red. (2) --root defaulted to . so a run from any other directory printed 0 checked, 0 RED and exited 0, the silent-green shape; the sibling script already anchored its root to the script. (3) #904 moved two numbers and left five sentences plus the test METHOD NAME saying four, with the WHY paragraph still claiming all four sites pause when the rollback has stopped since #823.
expected_outcome: Shapes widened, root anchored with a distinct exit code when nothing is seen, prose and method name corrected. Also: #904 decoupled the two counts and they are actually offset by two, so for the likeliest future edit both still move - decoupling was as wrong as equating; the fifth caller's provenance is bae1672 (#625b), not the two later commits that only edited its logging; unknown escapes are now excluded rather than mis-counted; the binding back-scan is bounded at the enclosing func; SIGPIPE and the importlib load are guarded. The selftest now COUNTS its checks - my own rewrite first printed a literal 13 while fixing a literal 8 - and exercises the resolver, which is where every gap lived. Registered in Tests/CISmoke/CLAUDE.md section 4 beside dead-needles.py.

decision: #906: a skipped step now says so - and adding a log line silently rewired three existing needles
reasoning: Deferred from the #902 review: releaseRecordRoute writes holders none, lowering and returns true, then downgradeToPlaybackAfterRecording can return silently at its already-playback guard. By the ladder's own law silence between two rungs is a DEATH, so a no-op read as a crash inside setCategory. The SKIPPED convention already existed in AudioEngine since #862b with the law written beside it; it had simply never reached this file. Both category moves now say it. THE SELF-INFLICTED HALF: the new line contains the substring the three ordering claims search for and stands EARLIER, so those claims would have been satisfied by the SKIPPED line even if the real rung moved after the call it names - a 367 weakening opened by my own diff, closed in the same commit by tightening the needles to the full rung text.
expected_outcome: A new log line is also a new NEEDLE: adding a line that contains an existing needle as a prefix changes every guard that searches for it. Also the first live proof of the #904 checker: count-pins printed pinned 12, actual 14 before this commit existed, catching in one cycle the drift that went unseen for thirteen when only CI was watching. The third silent return (guard isSessionConfigured) deliberately gets no line - it can only fire before the session exists at all.

decision: #907: a number on a SKIPPED step made the ladder tool call a healthy run a death
reasoning: #906 gave both category-move no-op guards a breadcrumb and wrote them NUMBERED (session: raise 1/2 SKIPPED). diag-ladder.py's LOG mode keeps the LAST n/N per ladder and has no notion of a skip, so a healthy TWO-OWNER run ended at 1/2 and the tool printed stopped before their last step - a DEATH AT THAT STEP - on exactly the path #888 exists to illuminate. Reproduced on a synthetic log both ways. It slipped because I drove only --source, which walks the EMITTERS in Sources and was correctly green; the two modes read different things. #907 also RETRACTS the #906 row's closing sentence: the third silent return (guard isSessionConfigured) does NOT only fire before the session exists - it also fires after a THROWN configureAudioSession, and only one of the three claim sites configures first, so the session can sit on .playAndRecord with nobody holding it while the log says holders none, lowering. It now has a line too, worded never configured; category left as-is because that path is a state defect, not a no-op. REVIEW (12 findings, three of them my own unmeasured claims): the LAW as first written was too general - unnumbered is right only where the skip precedes EVERY rung of its ladder. MicrophoneManager's mic: start REFUSED sits between 2/3 and 3/3 and yields a FALSE DEATH; my re-measurement goes further than the review, which called 2/3 SKIPPED the only spelling that stops it - it does not (the tool keeps the last n/N), and 3/3 SKIPPED reports a step that never ran. Mid-ladder NO source wording is honest, so the ban forbids no correct repair. Also fixed: two bare-return guards that exited the whole test method with no XCTFail (a rename would have skipped two tuples, the new ban and the count pin and reported GREEN); a 367 grading error where I called the AudioEngine scan a live counterweight when it selects ZERO lines there and three in AudioConfiguration; a false-red vector where the ban read the raw line so a trailing comment carrying 1/2 would redden a line with no number.
expected_outcome: A skipped step may be NUMBERED only when the ladder WALKS ON past it, AND only where the skip precedes every rung is unnumbered actually correct. Claim (c3) enforces the ban over both files; its AudioEngine half is honestly graded as a TRIPWIRE (0 lines selected there, 3 in AudioConfiguration), not a counterweight. Also pinned: ADJACENCY, because g<s<r is satisfied by lifting the emitter out of the else block - where it then fires on every SUCCESSFUL move - and both directions were measured (lifted tree: adjacency RED, ordering GREEN). Registered diag-ladder.py in Tests/CISmoke/CLAUDE.md section 4 with DRIVE BOTH MODES, ALWAYS. NEXT SLICE, named rather than left implicit: two cycles running, a WORDING change has compensated for a blind spot in scripts/diag-ladder.py. It needs one concept it lacks - a line that TERMINATES a ladder without ADVANCING it. Teaching it that makes every wording legal, removes the mic: start false death, and retires claim (c3) plus the law paragraph. Council question, own slice, own selftest.

decision: #908: the ladder tool learned a terminator - and its first draft turned a real death into a tidy end
reasoning: #907 named this as the next slice: two cycles running, a WORDING change had compensated for a blind spot in scripts/diag-ladder.py. It now knows a TERMINATOR - a line that ENDS a ladder without ADVANCING it - so mic: start REFUSED, which sits between 2/3 and 3/3, reads as ended instead of a false death. That is the case no source wording could fix (measured: 2/3 SKIPPED prints the same, 3/3 SKIPPED prints a tick for a step that never ran). THE EXPENSIVE HALF: the first draft also rescued NUMBERED skips, and AudioEngine's on 4/5 SKIPPED WALKS ON to on 5/5, so a log ending there is a death inside installTap - the isInputConnToConverter region the ladder exists for - and the tool printed ended, exit 0, telling the reader not to look there. My own selftest pinned that as correct (367 in pure form). Found by the mandatory reviewer, reproduced by me on a synthetic log.
